Solution 10[edit]

Q24 — Parallelogram with perpendicular projections Trigbash / vector geometry Answer A · 81

A parallelogram \(ABCD\) has area \(15\). Points \(P,Q\) are perpendicular projections of \(A,C\) onto diagonal \(BD\); points \(R,S\) are the projections of \(B,D\) onto diagonal \(AC\). We know \[ PQ=6,\qquad RS=8. \]

The longer diagonal \(BD=d\). We want \(d^2=m+n\sqrt p\) and then \(m+n+p\). Reconstructed arrangement of the diagonals and projections. \(O\) is their intersection. Dashed lines mark perpendicular projections. Step 1 — Introduce the diagonal lengths Set \[ AC=u,\qquad BD=v, \]

and let \(\theta\) be the acute angle between the diagonals. The length of an orthogonal projection is the original length multiplied by \(\cos\theta\). Therefore, \[ \boxed{u\cos\theta=6} \]

and \[ \boxed{v\cos\theta=8}. \]

Thus, \[ u=\frac6{\cos\theta}, \qquad v=\frac8{\cos\theta}. \]

Step 2 — Express the area in terms of the diagonals A parallelogram with diagonals \(u,v\) meeting at angle \(\theta\) has area \[ \boxed{K=\frac12uv\sin\theta}. \]

To see this, the diagonals bisect each other, dividing the parallelogram into four triangles, each with area \(\frac18uv\sin\theta\). Since \(K=15\), \[ 15=\frac12 \cdot\frac6{\cos\theta} \cdot\frac8{\cos\theta} \sin\theta. \]

Simplify: \[ 15=\frac{24\sin\theta}{\cos^2\theta}. \]

Hence, \[ \boxed{\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos^2\theta}=\frac58}. \]

Step 3 — Turn the trigonometry into a quadratic Let \[ t=\frac1{\cos^2\theta}. \]

Then \[ \sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta =1-\frac1t. \]

Square the preceding equation: \[ \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^4\theta} =\frac{25}{64}. \]

The left side is \[ \left(1-\frac1t\right)t^2=t^2-t. \]

Therefore, \[ t^2-t=\frac{25}{64}. \]

Multiply by \(64\): \[ 64t^2-64t-25=0. \]

Use the quadratic formula: \[ t=\frac{64\pm\sqrt{64^2+4(64)(25)}}{128}. \]

The discriminant simplifies to \[ 10496=256\cdot41. \]

Thus, \[ t=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{41}}8. \]

Since \(t=1/\cos^2\theta\ge1\), we take \[ \boxed{t=\frac{4+\sqrt{41}}8}. \]
